summary.text: Christine Marsh is the Democratic candidate for Arizona State Senate District 5 in the November 3, 2026 general election, where she faces No Labels Party candidate Jason LaForest in a race with no incumbent.
A retired teacher who was named Arizona's Teacher of the Year in 2016, she previously served in the Arizona State Senate from 2023 to 2025.

paragraphs.text: Marsh graduated from Chaparral High School, earned a bachelor's degree in English literature from the University of California, Los Angeles, in 1989, and received a master's degree in educational leadership and administration from Grand Canyon University in 2016, according to Ballotpedia.
In a Ballotpedia survey, she described herself as a mother, foster mother and retired teacher with 32 years of experience, and said she attended UCLA on a track scholarship.
She said she now works part-time as a caregiver.
Marsh lost the 2018 general election for Arizona State Senate District 28 to incumbent Kate Brophy McGee, then defeated Brophy McGee in the November 3, 2020 rematch.
She assumed office as senator for District 4 on January 9, 2023, and left office on January 13, 2025, after Carine Werner defeated her in the November 5, 2024 general election.

Ballotpedia lists her committee assignments in 2023 and 2024 as the Senate Education and Transportation Committee, the Senate Judiciary and Elections Committee, and the Transportation and Technology Committee.
In the survey, Marsh said she lost her youngest son to an accidental fentanyl overdose and that during her first session she championed a bill to legalize fentanyl testing strips.
She said combating the opioid epidemic would remain a legislative priority, and her campaign messages emphasized public education, public transportation and access to the ballot.
She listed endorsements from Arizona List, AFSCME, Professional Firefighters of Arizona, UFCW and the Teamsters, among others.
